title: Syntax-Diversified Unlearning: Evaluating Data-Side Interventions for Reducing Worst-Case Leakage

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to test the hypothesis that syntactic diversification of forget queries reduces worst-case sampling leakage and benign relearning vulnerability in LLM unlearning. Paper [7] explicitly investigates the role of syntax in benign relearning failures, demonstrating that syntactic similarity drives unlearning fragility. This aligns with the contribution's purpose of exploring syntactic diversification as a mitigation strategy for relearning vulnerability. Paper [6] also discusses benign relearning attacks but attributes them to topical relevance rather than syntax, making it less directly aligned. Therefore, paper [7] covers the purpose.

### Mechanism
The contribution implements a paraphrase-based augmentation pipeline that adds syntactically diverse variants of forget queries to the forget set during NPO unlearning. Paper [26] introduces syntactically controlled paraphrase networks (SCPNs) to generate syntactically diverse paraphrases, which is substantively equivalent to the mechanism described here. Although SCPNs are used for adversarial example generation rather than unlearning, the underlying primitive — syntactic paraphrasing for augmentation — is identical. Thus, paper [26] covers the mechanism.

### Evaluation
The contribution evaluates via leak@32 worst-case sampling leakage and relearning vulnerability on TOFU forget10 using Negative Preference Optimization (NPO). Paper [17] introduces NPO as a method for LLM unlearning and evaluates it on similar metrics (e.g., unlearning effectiveness and model utility). Paper [14] introduces the TOFU benchmark, which includes forget10, and paper [9] critiques existing benchmarks for unlearning robustness. Since the evaluation design (NPO-based metrics and TOFU forget10) is reused from prior work, the evaluation is covered by papers [17] and [14].

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of LLM machine unlearning. Papers [1], [2], [4], [5], [6], [7], [8], [9], [10], [11], [13], [14], [15], [17], and [18] all address LLM unlearning, making this domain well-established. Therefore, the domain is covered.
